title: How to Clear a Clogged Bathtub Drain: Drain Snake Use, Stopper Inspection, and Linkage Adjustment (This Old House)
summary: This This Old House segment walks through diagnosing and clearing a clogged bathtub drain using a homeowner-grade drain snake, followed by inspecting and replacing a worn stopper and correcting the trip-lever linkage. The host demonstrates accessing the drain plate, feeding the snake through the overflow, feeling for resistance, and withdrawing to dislodge the blockage. After partial clearing, they test drainage with water, observe a possible stopper misalignment via surface water staining, replace the stopper assembly, adjust the linkage and plunger height, reseal with screws, and perform a final drain test which confirms improved flow and proper operation.
topics: Maintain exposed wire length (about six inches)
Lock and rotate drum to feed snake
Push snake through trap toward obstruction
Withdraw and re-feed to extend reach
Identify brass vs. discolored water stains
Align stopper linkage via depth of water stand
Tighten stopper thread and lock nut

sections.title: Access and remove the drain plate
sections.description: The initial step is to remove the plate covering the drain to expose the stopper and access the internal components.

sections.title: Feed the homeowner-grade drain snake into the overflow
sections.description: A homeowner version of a drain snake is introduced. The wire is advanced down the overflow, with the wire length limited to a short exposed portion, while the drum is rotated and the wire pushed steadily into the drain.

sections.title: Through-trap feeding, withdrawal, and water test
sections.description: The host notes progress through the trap, adjusts the exposed wire, and then tests the drain by running water to gauge clearing progress.

sections.title: Stopper/stats inspection and lean toward replacement
sections.description: Attention turns to the stopper area: water stains indicate the lever had been sitting in a fixed position, suggesting the linkage could be the root cause of the problem and prompting stopper replacement.

sections.title: Adjusting trip-lever linkage and plunger height
sections.description: The technician aligns the linkage by adjusting the plunger height to match the observed water stand depth, and tightens the lock nut to secure the setting.

sections.title: Reassembly and final drainage test
sections.description: The stopper assembly is reinstalled, and a final test confirms the drain opens and remains blocked as designed when the lever is engaged, indicating successful restoration of function.

featured_techniques.technique: Insertion and advancement of a homeowner drain snake through the bathtub overflow to clear a clog
Controlled feeding with drum rotation and maintaining a short exposed wire length
Withdrawal and back-feeding of the snake to extend reach toward obstruction
Drain-flow verification after partial clearing to assess improvement
Diagnosis of a misaligned stopper/linkage via water-stain evidence
Adjusting stopper linkage by raising the plunger and tightening the lock nut
Final reassembly and verification test of the stopper and drain function
